name: DonutChart
whenToUse: Parts of one whole, up to 7: storage by environment, plan mix, traffic by source.
When the total matters too — it sits in the center.

whenNotToUse.text: Comparing values that aren’t parts of a whole
More than 7 parts, or many tiny slices

anatomy.description: name and value per slice; `layout` vertical/horizontal.

do.caption: Three parts of one total, named in the legend.
do.example:
<DonutChart
  data={[{ label: 'Production', value: 62 }, { label: 'Staging', value: 24 }, { label: 'Dev', value: 14 }]}
  unit=" GB"
  layout="horizontal"
  height={160}
  ariaLabel="Storage by environment: production 62 GB of 100 GB."
/>

dont.caption: Seven similar slices: angles this close can’t be compared — a sorted bar chart can.
dont.example:
<DonutChart
  data={[
    { label: 'eu-west-1', value: 22 }, { label: 'eu-central-1', value: 18 }, { label: 'us-east-1', value: 16 },
    { label: 'us-west-2', value: 14 }, { label: 'ap-south-1', value: 11 }, { label: 'ap-southeast-1', value: 10 }, { label: 'sa-east-1', value: 9 },
  ]}
  unit="%"
  layout="horizontal"
  height={160}
  ariaLabel="Traffic by region."
/>

a11y: `ariaLabel` states the takeaway; the legend repeats every name and value as text.
Slice colors aren’t the only cue — the legend order matches the ring.

props.name: thickness
props.description: Ring band width: "default" (thicker) or "thin" (a slim indicator ring).
